text: A subgraph deployed to Studio is synced and queryable by you, but free, rate-limited, and invisible to anyone else. Making it public is a separate, deliberate step called publishing.
It's triggered from the same Studio dashboard, with the Publish button.
Clicking it opens a modal confirming which network, and whether to add curation signal — GRT staked on this subgraph to economically signal indexers it's worth indexing.
Once published and synced, the subgraph gets a real card in Graph Explorer, with live query volume and signal — and the Query button is the entire point of everything built so far.
That leads to the actual production endpoint: a base URL, your API key, and the subgraph's own ID.
Querying is a standard GraphQL POST, and it's where the schema from Lesson 13 pays off — first, orderBy, orderDirection, and where are all generated automatically.
That closes the loop on The Graph. Next up, Lesson 16 compares this managed path against running a custom indexer yourself.
